function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick guide to help you find the best place to order a cake—whether it’s for a birthday, wedding, corporate event, or just a sweet treat. | Category | What to Look For | How to Find It | |----------|------------------|----------------| | **Local Bakeries** | • Fresh, made‑to‑order.
• Custom designs & flavors.
• Often offer gluten‑free, vegan, or allergy‑friendly options. | • Google “cake shop near me” or “custom cakes in [your city].”
• Yelp, TripAdvisor, or local food blogs.
• Ask friends/family for recommendations. | | **National Chains** | • Consistent quality & branding.
• Usually have a wide range of standard flavors and sizes.
• Some offer online customization. | • Check the chain’s website (e.g., Baskin‑Robbins, Mrs. Fields).
• Use their store locator to find a nearby outlet. | | **Online Marketplaces** | • Curated selection from multiple bakers.
• Reviews & ratings from other customers.
• Delivery across state lines (great for gifts). | • Goldbelly.com – great for specialty or artisanal cakes.
• Etsy – find local artisans who ship nationwide. | | **Food Delivery Apps** | • Same‑day delivery from local restaurants & bakeries.
• Real‑time tracking & customer support.
• Often have promo codes. | • Uber Eats, DoorDash, Postmates, Grubhub.
• Search “cakes” or “desserts” in the app. | | **Grocery Store Delivery** | • Convenient if you’re already shopping there.
• Many stores now offer bakery sections that ship. | • Walmart Grocery, Kroger, Safeway, Target (via Shipt).
• Check the “Bakery” section on the store’s delivery app. | | **Specialty Cake Shops** | • Unique themes (e.g., wedding cakes, novelty cakes).
• Often offer design consultations. | • Search “wedding cake shop” or “novelty cake” + your city.
• Look for shops that showcase portfolios online. | ### Tips for Ordering 1. **Plan Ahead** * Most custom cakes require at least 1–2 weeks’ notice. * For same‑day delivery, place the order at least 24 hours in advance. 2. **Specify Dietary Needs Early** * Gluten‑free, nut‑free, dairy‑free, vegan, or keto options. * Confirm ingredient lists and allergen information. 3. **Check Reviews & Ratings** * Look for recent feedback on taste, appearance, and delivery reliability. * Pay attention to comments about packaging and temperature control. 4. **Ask About Packaging & Shipping** * Does the bakery use insulated boxes or gel packs? * Will they deliver on a specific date/time window? 5. **Confirm Payment & Cancellation Policies** * Some places require a deposit for custom orders. * Know the refund policy if the cake doesn’t arrive on time or looks off. 6. **Use Promo Codes & Loyalty Programs** * Many delivery apps offer first‑order discounts. * Local bakeries sometimes have loyalty cards or referral bonuses. 7. **Consider the Occasion** * For weddings or large events, book a tasting session if possible. * For birthdays or small gatherings, a simple “birthday cake” order may suffice. ### Quick Start Checklist - [ ] Decide on cake size & flavor. - [ ] Choose a delivery method (local bakery, app, grocery). - [ ] Place order 1–2 weeks ahead (or 24 hrs for same‑day). - [ ] Verify delivery address & time slot. - [ ] Double‑check dietary requirements. - [ ] Keep the receipt & contact info handy for follow‑up. --- #### Example Order Flow (Using a Food Delivery App) 1. Open the app → Search “cakes.” 2. Filter by “Customizable” or “Gluten‑Free.” 3. Select a bakery with high ratings. 4. Choose a pre‑made cake or tap “Customize.” 5. Add any special instructions (e.g., “no nuts,” “birthday message”). 6. Review the total cost (delivery fee + tip). 7. Confirm the delivery address & time. 8. Pay & track the order until it arrives. Feel free to let me know what kind of cake you’re looking for (flavor, size, occasion), and I can narrow down the best local options for you!
